chapter: Early music and the Olympia band
title: Bands she heard before marriage; Charlie Bocage and his banjo song
summary: She recalls a band from over the river and Charlie Bocage, who played little banjo and sang a song about shoes.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section's changing role

blocks.x: Well, I wanted to ask you about, when you first started, you know, listening to music, you say you heard piano players like Sonny Swan?
Did you hear any bands before you met your husband? Did you hear many bands before you met your husband?

Did you listen to music? Oh, yeah, there was... Some band came from over the river, but I can't place them. And they was a fine band, too. They was from over the river. They was with, uh, how do you call that fellow? Oh, Charlie Bokauer, the Bokauer's. Oh, I know them. Yeah, I heard them, you know. They had Peter Bokauer, Charlie Bokauer. I knew all of them. Poor, fine people. Charlie's still living.
I haven't seen him in a long time, but they tell me...

He's still living. He lost his wife. He was a personal friend of ours. He lost his wife. And, uh, then I believe some of the relatives got killed under that bridge when they was fishing. Some of them, Charlie Bokauer. You don't know Charlie Bokauer?

He's a little short fellow, you know. And now he gave up music a long time. He used to play, uh, guitar. And he used to come home all the time and sing. And they used to make him sing that, because there was one of the girls around used to always have, uh, slippers on. And Charlie would sing a song about, uh, uh, don't send me a pose, it's shoes what I need. And, uh, Charlie Bokauer used to sing that. That was his great song on his banjo. You know, the little round banjo. You know how they had that little banjo? Charlie used to play that and sing.
And that's the kind of stuff we want. Now you strike it as great.

And, uh, don't send me, uh, don't send me roses. In shoes is what I need. That was Charlie's great song. I told Luciana, I think it was one day, uh, last week, that I'm going to try to see if I can find him, you know. He was always his sister, jolly fella, you know. And, uh, one of his sons, I think, wait where he was, Henry. He breaks that LSU. Oh, yeah. But anyway, and, uh, they had, uh, Adolph Ducanger used to play piano with him. One, uh, when he played at the Cadillac. That was a nightclub right there, Ramport.
